reading.identification: A one-storey 16th-17th century Flemish brick service/almshouse range in Ghent's Graslei-Patershol quarter, presenting its blank-plinthed garden elevation to a sett footpath, with stone cross-mullioned windows, green shutters and a steep clay pantile roof.
reading.notes: Set A (3D tiles) is degraded to unreadable smears over the target and was used ONLY to confirm ridge orientation; every wall-level field comes from set B image _1. Scale derived from frontage_width_m 10.3 spanning ~505 px in the magenta box (~49 px/m at wall plane): eaves ~5.0 m, ridge ~8.5 m, consistent with the 9.2 m height datum. That settles storeys at 1 tall storey + attic, not 2 — a single window band with blank brick beneath it down to the hedge. The pedestrian in _1 stands forward of the wall plane and was not used for scale. Bays: left cross-wing gable (small attic light, stone corbels visible in _0) plus three windows; the right two are clearly stone cross-divided (kruiskozijn), the left one a simpler tall opening. Shutters read as set back behind the stone frame with a pronounced left-jamb shadow, hence deep reveal class. Trim mapped to 'marble' as the nearest stone dielectric proxy for Balegem-type sandstone dressings; if the generator prefers a lower permittivity, concrete is the acceptable fallback. roughness_mm 7 is INFERRED from visible hand-moulded brick with weathered recessed joints — no image measures RMS height; the brick relief must stay a roughness/scattering coefficient and never be meshed, since 1-10 cm facets at 1.07 cm wavelength produce specular garbage. Geometry budget belongs on the window reveals, stone mullions/transoms and sills, the eaves line, the two chimneys and the cross-wing gable silhouette — these are the only >10 cm features on an otherwise blank wall and they carry the entire off-specular return at street level. Ground floor marked blank on the evidence of the outlined frontage only; a door may exist behind the hedge. Clutter: clipped beech hedge along the full frontage, grass/gravel verge, green utility cabinet at the right end. NO vehicles — fronting way is highway=path, surface=sett, car_access=none. Do not let a generic parked-car rule touch this frontage.
